entries.title: Culpable homicide
entries.analysis: The definition is relocated. Compare the elements of intention and knowledge in the applicable text.

entries.title: Definition of murder
entries.analysis: The definition and exceptions remain distinct from the punishment provision; check the applicable exceptions.

entries.title: Punishment for murder
entries.analysis: The general punishment is addressed in subsection (1); subsection (2) separately addresses a specified group-based form of murder. Do not treat the additional subsection as an exact IPC counterpart.

entries.title: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
entries.analysis: The punishment framework changes. Compare the intention and knowledge limbs separately.

entries.title: Death caused by negligence
entries.analysis: The ordinary maximum custodial term increases from two to five years; a separate two-year maximum applies to registered medical practitioners performing medical procedures under the stated conditions.

entries.title: Negligent driving and failure to report
entries.analysis: A distinct subsection addresses specified driving and reporting circumstances. The initial commencement notification excluded this subsection; verify any later commencement notification before applying it.

entries.title: Attempt to murder
entries.analysis: The provision is relocated with changes including the treatment of an attempt by a life convict. Verify the applicable subsection.

entries.title: Attempt to commit culpable homicide
entries.analysis: Compare the definition and the separate punishment limb where hurt results.

entries.title: Definition of hurt
entries.analysis: The definition is relocated; distinguish it from the provision punishing voluntary hurt.

entries.title: Voluntarily causing hurt
entries.analysis: Definition and punishment are brought together in one section, with distinct subsections. Compare the penalty provisions.

entries.title: Definition of grievous hurt
entries.analysis: The statutory categories require comparison; the duration criterion in the final category changes from twenty to fifteen days.

entries.title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt
entries.analysis: Definition and punishment are consolidated, with additional aggravated circumstances addressed in later subsections. Not every BNS subsection corresponds to an IPC provision.

entries.title: Organised crime
entries.analysis: A dedicated BNS offence; no direct IPC section in the correspondence table. Other special enactments may address overlapping conduct.

entries.title: Petty organised crime
entries.analysis: A dedicated BNS provision. The absence of a direct IPC counterpart does not imply that underlying conduct was lawful before BNS.

entries.title: Theft
entries.analysis: Definition and punishment share a section. BNS introduces a conditional community-service rule for certain first convictions involving low-value stolen property and restoration; check all statutory conditions.

entries.title: Snatching
entries.analysis: A separate BNS offence; conduct may previously have fallen under other offences depending on facts.

entries.title: Theft in specified locations
entries.analysis: The BNS provision expressly addresses additional locations or property categories. Check the specific clause.

entries.title: Theft by clerk or servant
entries.analysis: The corresponding provision concerns theft by a clerk or servant of property in the master's possession.

entries.title: Extortion
entries.analysis: Definition, ordinary punishment and aggravated forms are consolidated. The ordered section lists align with the subsection correspondences; select the specific limb.

entries.title: Criminal breach of trust
entries.analysis: Definition and different punishment categories are consolidated. Ordinary maximum imprisonment changes from three to five years; verify the specific category.

entries.title: Stolen property and receiving offences
entries.analysis: Separate IPC provisions are consolidated into distinct subsections. Check the applicable elements and punishment.

entries.title: Cheating
entries.analysis: Definition and different punishment limbs are grouped together. Ordinary cheating has an increased maximum term; the dishonest inducement to deliver property is addressed separately in subsection (4).

entries.title: Cheating by personation
entries.analysis: Definition and punishment are consolidated; compare the punishment provisions.
